<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 295d8067c1e1e7719d70e82ff118157b6539e7a6`.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `defaultValue (symbol, 42 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **36** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 295d8067c1e1e7719d70e82ff118157b6539e7a6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b5ba7cce90fb9f4ef8ab372c43cae18b3e3cfe34` — the merge of head `716e75f6cf90efa5e3ed382f5159ae2c31cb30c6` into base `295d8067c1e1e7719d70e82ff118157b6539e7a6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b5ba7cce90fb9f4ef8ab372c43cae18b3e3cfe34 && git checkout b5ba7cce90fb9f4ef8ab372c43cae18b3e3cfe34
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 295d8067c1e1e7719d70e82ff118157b6539e7a6 716e75f6cf90efa5e3ed382f5159ae2c31cb30c6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 295d8067c1e1e7719d70e82ff118157b6539e7a6 && git merge --no-ff 716e75f6cf90efa5e3ed382f5159ae2c31cb30c6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 295d8067c1e1e7719d70e82ff118157b6539e7a6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 295d8067c1e1e7719d70e82ff118157b6539e7a6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `716e75f6cf90efa5e3ed382f5159ae2c31cb30c6`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Read: card #32435 body and all five comments (triage 6799178291, serial note 6807063044, claim 6811667554, claim amendment 6811914386, os-dev-report 6813116456); PR #32523 body, its 10-file list and the net diff against `main`; the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read at the head, not reviewed.

Check-runs on the head, read 2026-11-12T03:20Z: 51 check-runs, all completed: 35 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed, 0 running. Success includes Build Core, Test Core (8 of 8 shards and the roll-up), Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), every Lint family, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI. The skipped ones are path-filtered or opt-in jobs (UI build and test shards, docs build, temporal conformance, queue verdicts, upgrade harness, tarball smoke).

Public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. `describe_object` over HTTP (`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`) gains per field `readonly`, `system` (always, booleans), `options` (value + label, on a field whose served definition carries an `options` array), `defaultValue` (when declared), and per object `validations`. RIGHT: additive. `name`, `type`, `label`, `required`, the object's `name`, `label`, `enableFeatures` are computed by the same expressions as on `main`; `fields` stays an array, which `validate_expression` depends on.
2. `describe_object` over stdio (`packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts`) gains the same keys. RIGHT, same reasoning.
3. The `objectstack://objects/{objectName}` resource gains the same keys. RIGHT, and declared: it now serialises the one exported `describeServedObject` the stdio tool returns, so #25245's pin (`mcp-server-runtime.merged-object-resources.test.ts` line 153, untouched) holds by construction. The amendment's ruling A covers the file.
4. Twin parity. The two `describeServedObject` bodies (and `describedOptions`, `describedRules`, `describedRule`, depth 10) are the same code token for token, and each reads the object through its transport's ADR-0106 view (`callerObjectView` on stdio, `servedToCaller` over HTTP, both unchanged by this diff). Same caller, same object: same answer. RIGHT. Parity rests on two parallel suites with the same expectations; no single test compares the twins (see nit N4).
5. Hidden narrowing: none. No key dropped or renamed; a `null` answer for an unreadable or unknown object is unchanged; the tool handler serialises the bridge's answer whole (`textResult(def)`), so no second projection clips or reorders it.
6. Package exports: `describeServedObject` and `ServedObjectDef` are exported from the module, not from `packages/mcp/src/index.ts`. No new package-level API. RIGHT.
7. The tool description (`mcp-http-tools.ts`) states the new shape. Each sentence checked against the code: `readonly` "a write to it is dropped" matches `stripReadonlyFields` on both write paths; `options` "send the value" matches the write door; `validations` "active" matches `rule-validator.ts` (`active !== false`, and a conditional branch with `active: false` is skipped, as here); the stated defaults `error` and `[insert, update]` match `ValidationRuleSchema`; `field` / `fields` are the only rule keys that name fields in the six variants.

Design reading of the same changes (declaration face: no ④ section; the findings are kept here).

Tried to break it; every item is against the tree at the head.

`packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts` and `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` (the twin projections): HOLD.
- FLS-denied field through `options` / `defaultValue`: the field's whole entry is deleted before the projection runs, so neither key exists for it. A readable field's `defaultValue` that mentions a denied name is deleted by the mask (`defaultValue: expression`), and an option's `visibleWhen` is not served at all.
- Denied field through a rule's `fields`, condition or message: the mask drops the rule entry whole on any mention, nested branches included; the projection additionally never serves `condition`, `when`, `regex`, `format`, `schema`, `transitions`, `initialStates`. Both suites pin "no `record.` text" and "the denied name is no token of the answer", on the real security layer over HTTP.
- Formula text: a field's `expression` is not a served key; `bonus_formula` in the shared case table is served with no expression.
- Object not readable by the caller, posture that cannot be evaluated, emptied projection: unchanged (`undefined` / coded refusal) and upstream of the projection.
- Tenant / environment scoping: the served object is resolved per request and per environment by code this diff does not touch.
- Inactive rules: left out, at top level and in a conditional branch, as the engine runs them.
- Picklist-bound field: served with the list's resolved options (pinned by the option-labels suite, equal to `optionFieldsOf`).
- Unmasked postures (no `security` service, D4-exempt caller, ADR-0106 D6 "undetermined"): the answer is unmasked exactly where `/meta` is. The widening rides that posture and adds no new one.

Findings:
- N1 (nit, follow-up card owed): `readonly` is the declared flag alone. The engine drops a caller's write to `readonly: true` OR a runtime-owned type (`isRuntimeOwnedField`, `RUNTIME_OWNED_FIELD_TYPES` in `@objectstack/spec/data`, today `autonumber`), and never stores a `formula` from the payload. A hand-authored `{ type: 'autonumber' }` literal (the `Field.autonumber` builder injects the flag, a literal does not) and every formula field are served `readonly: false`. Nothing published is false (the description defines what `readonly: true` means, and `type` is served), so it is a nit, but it is the card's own complaint ("looks writable") for that residue. One line per twin closes it.
- N2 (nit, follow-up): `readonly` says nothing of the caller's EDIT permission. A field the caller may read but not edit is served `readonly: false`, and the write is refused by FLS. The card asks for "what a write needs, under the caller's FLS"; this diff delivers the read half. Same card as N1 or its own.
- N3 (nit, prose): `mcp-http-tools.ts`, the `optionFieldsOf` member's jsdoc still ends "so `describe_object` serves what it served before". The diff makes that clause false. Comment only.
- N4 (nit): no single test compares the two twins' answers; a later edit to one body is caught only if the matching expectation in the other suite is also edited. Each docblock names the other. Accepted as the repo's existing twin pattern for these bridges.
- N5 (nit): `defaultValue` is served as declared, so it may be a token (`NOW()`, `current_user`) or a CEL envelope, not always a literal. The description's "when an insert applies one" is true; an agent should omit the field, not copy the value. A phrase in the description would say so.

`packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts`: HOLDS. `describeObject` returns the shared projection over `servedView.getObject`, unchanged reads.

`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`: HOLDS (description only; see N3, N5).

Tests, as evidence: the two `[#32435]` describes pin the member case and an unrestricted CONTROL (byte-equal to a deployment with no security service); three old-shape pins were moved to the new shape, none deleted or weakened. The stdio suite covers `state_machine` and `conditional`; the HTTP suite does not, and relies on the identical body.

No must-fix. No should-fix.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/32435-describe-object-write-facts.md`: `@objectstack/mcp` patch, `@objectstack/runtime` patch. Both moved packages are named and no other package's source moves. RIGHT under AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes patch, and a non-protocol widening ships patch.
- `Clause-②: yes`, line-initial in the PR body and the changeset body, no arm. RIGHT: a public answer widens, nothing narrows, so not BREAKING and no ADR-0087 marker is owed.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`. RIGHT: no spec file moves and nothing a metadata author can write changes.
- `Skills-docs: none`. RIGHT on the claim it makes: no page under `content/docs/**` or `skills/**` states the four-key field shape (the hits name the tool or its purpose only). `packages/mcp/README.md` line 113 ("Object schema: fields + features") and line 186 are loose enough to stay true.
- Changeset prose against the diff, sentence by sentence: accurate, including "a picklist-bound field included" (the registry writes the list's resolved options onto the served field) and "a rule that names such a field anywhere is not described" (`ruleEntries` in `object-schema-fls-references.ts` drops the entry on any identifier-token mention, message and nested `then` / `otherwise` included).

### ③ Boundary flags

PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no relay-bypass note is owed.

Deviations in os-dev-report 6813116456:
- File surface widened to `packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts`: ANSWERED by claim amendment 6811914386 (ruling A). The diff in that file is the projection and the resource's call of it, nothing else.
- PR assignee `os-bill` rides `pr_create`: ANSWERED, process only, no contract effect. For the seat to confirm against `os-dev.md` rule 2.

Out-of-scope findings the report carries with `carrier: none`:
- A rule message naming a hidden field by its LABEL is served: ANSWERED. It is ADR-0106's stated identifier-token reading, the same body the `/meta` object door serves this caller; not new here.
- Computed fields without a declared `readonly` are served `readonly: false`: ANSWERED as nit N1, which owes a follow-up card, not "noted".
- Rule messages are served as stored (untranslated): ANSWERED, accepted; the description says "the message is what a refused write answers", which a translated refusal makes approximate. Fold into the N1 card or its own.

Report accuracy: `line_budget` says "tests 6 files"; the diff and the report's own `files_changed` carry five. No contract effect.

Flag to the seat: the claim's file surface for `mcp-http-tools.ts` is "the `describe_object` description only", which is why nit N3 (a jsdoc in the same file) was left; it needs a surface line if fixed here.

Security: no security finding. `security_findings: none` in the report holds on my reading.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-6i6ij5`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CaP1iy4RSEQbW6177G`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 维护者速读

1. 改了什么：MCP 的 `describe_object`（HTTP 与 stdio 两种传输）和 `objectstack://objects/{name}` 资源，现在按调用者可见范围给出每个字段的选项（值+标签）、默认值、`readonly`/`system`，以及对象上启用的校验规则（名称、类型、提示语、作用字段，不含表达式）。
2. 为什么改：AI 代理写记录前先读这个工具，以前只有名称/类型/标签/必填，选择字段只能猜值、被拒、再重试。
3. 风险与回滚：只加字段不删字段；字段级权限隐藏的字段及提到它的规则一律不出现；回滚即还原本 PR。
4. 先看：`packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts` 新的共享投影 `describeServedObject`，以及 `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` 的孪生实现。
5. 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp exec vitest run src/stdio-data-bridge.object-schema-mask.test.ts`，预期全部通过。
6. 需要你做的：无，席位落地（非 BREAKING、非受管面、623 行）。

席位意见：ACCEPT。契约审查 PASS（6813417317，无必改、无应改）；公式/自动编号/无编辑权的字段仍显示可写等余项立为 #32530。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · domain:server#2 · head `716e75f6cf90efa5e3ed382f5159ae2c31cb30c6` · 2026-11-12T03:24Z

- **形态:** 10 files (+568/−55): the shared projection in `mcp-server-runtime.ts` (claim amendment ruling A), the two `describeObject` bridges, the `describe_object` description, five test files, one changeset (`patch` on `@objectstack/mcp` and `@objectstack/runtime`). Inside the claimed surface (6811667554 + amendment). Not governed (`check-governed-merges --pr 32523`: 0 of 10 paths, 623 ≤ 3000). Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay).
- **前提实测:** report 6813116456: both bridges red on `main` for the new keys, green with the fix; ablation three times, each red then restored. Step 0 overlap with seat B's #32437/#32438: none on the describe_object block (B confirmed).
- **门禁 check-runs:** head `716e75f6`: 35 success, 16 skipped, 0 failure/pending; `mergeable_state: clean`; `check-expected-skips --pr 32523`: OK. K = 5 (base `295d8067`).
- **接受的偏差:** contract review 6813417317 at the declaration face's tier (`TIER_DEFAULT`: no review-face path; `Clause-②: yes` with no narrowing arm), PASS. Assignee riding `pr_create` is process only. Report's "tests 6 files" is five.
- **范围外去向:** N1 (formula / runtime-owned fields served `readonly: false`), N2 (edit permission not reflected), N3 (stale `optionFieldsOf` jsdoc), N5 (`defaultValue` may be a token) → #32530. N4 (no cross-twin parity test) accepted as the bridges' existing twin pattern. Security: none.
- **落地条款:** `Fixes #32435`; not BREAKING (`Clause-②: yes`); seat lands: `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` after this record.
